record.paper_title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations: Status and open questions
record.original_question: How can experimental measurements and theoretical calculations distinguish correlations caused by initial-state effects from correlations generated by collective final-state evolution in relativistic heavy-ion collisions?

evidence.quote:
• What are the prospects for experimentally and/or theoretically distinguishing
between initial-state and collective effects?

The extensive
factorization tests of two-particle correlations (Vn∆) over a large range of trigger and
associated particle transverse momentum as carried out by the LHC collaborations are
useful to distinguish bulk anisotropies from other/non-flow contributions, as well as
to study flow fluctuations.

artifact.self_contained_problem: In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the azimuthal distribution of produced particles in the transverse plane is commonly expanded in a Fourier series, and two-particle azimuthal correlations are characterized by harmonic coefficients V_{n\\Delta}(p_T^a, p_T^t) defined for trigger and associated transverse momenta p_T^t and p_T^a. These correlations receive contributions from (i) initial-state effects, namely fluctuations of the geometry and density of the colliding nuclear matter at the time of impact (e.g., participant nucleon positions, color-charge fluctuations, gluon-saturation-induced correlations), and (ii) collective final-state effects, namely the hydrodynamic and hadronic-rescattering response of the produced quark-gluon medium that maps initial spatial anisotropies \\epsilon_n into momentum-space anisotropies v_n.\n\nFormulate concrete experimental observables and/or theoretical procedures that can unambiguously distinguish the contribution of initial-state correlations from the contribution of collective final-state evolution to measured multi-particle azimuthal correlations. In particular, identify observables (such as factorization tests of V_{n\\Delta} into single-particle harmonics v_n(p_T^t) v_n(p_T^a), system-size and centrality dependence, longitudinal decorrelation, multi-particle cumulants, or correlations between particles separated by large pseudorapidity gaps) whose behavior under purely initial-state correlation models versus hydrodynamic-response models is qualitatively or quantitatively different, and specify under what conditions such a separation is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing conceptual/phenomenological question in the heavy-ion community. While significant progress has been made (e.g., factorization-breaking studies of V_{n\\Delta}, longitudinal decorrelation measurements, small-system collectivity studies at RHIC and LHC, and IP-Glasma+hydrodynamic frameworks), no fully model-independent procedure has been established to cleanly separate initial-state from final-state collective contributions, especially in small collision systems. The question remains an active area of research as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations
status_evidence.snippet: What are the prospects for experimentally and/or theoretically distinguishing between initial-state and collective effects?
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open one in the heavy-ion community.

status_evidence.title: Small system collectivity reviews (post-2020)
status_evidence.snippet: Disentangling initial-state momentum correlations from final-state hydrodynamic flow in small systems remains an outstanding challenge.
status_evidence.claim: The disentanglement problem is still open, particularly in small systems.
